To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) genetic and non-genetical factors are important in human aging and health; (2) the role of genetic and non- genetic factors in aging and longevity is complex and requires a systems approach to be understood; and (3) the role of environmental factors is not well understood and requires further research.

(1) aging is associated with a progressive loss of immune function; (2) the loss of immune function is due, in part, to an increase in the number of senescent cells; (3) senescent cells secrete a variety of pro-inflammatory cytokines and other factors that contribute to a pro-inflammatory phenotype of the aging immune system; (4) the pro-inflammatory phenotype is associated with an increased risk of infections; (5) infections are associated with increased risk of mortality

(1) the age-related decline of immune function is associated with the development of infections and cancer in the elderly; (2) immunological interventions, including vaccination, are effective in preventing infections in the elderly, and may be useful in preventing cancer in the future; (3) a better understanding of the mechanisms of aging, and of the mechanisms of immunological interventions, will help to develop more effective and safer immunological interventions in the future.
